Let me analyze the code: 1. The HTML has CSS with a selector `.control.triggered + .section:has(.status.alert) .box.super.special` which sets various CSS custom properties. 2. The body has `data-mode="dark"` but wait - the selector is `html[data-mode="dark"]` but the body has `data-mode="dark"`, not the html element. So the dark mode CSS variables won't apply from the `html[data-mode="dark"]` rule. Wait, let me re-read. The body has `data-mode="dark"`, but the CSS rule is `html[data-mode="dark"]`. So this rule won't match. 3. The main CSS selector `.control.triggered + .section:has(.status.alert) .box.super.special` - let's check if it matches: - `.control.triggered` - yes, there's `
` - `+ .section` - the `.section` is the next sibling of `.control.triggered` - yes - `:has(.status.alert)` - the `.section` contains `.status.alert` - yes - `.box.super.special` - inside `.section`, there's `
` - yes So this CSS rule applies and sets the CSS custom properties. 4. The JavaScript then applies styles asynchronously: - First it waits 500ms with `delay(500)` - Then it calls `nestedFlow(0)` which applies `styleSteps[0]` - After that resolves, it waits 100ms and then calls `nestedFlow(1)` which applies `styleSteps[1]` - After that resolves, it waits 100ms and then calls `nestedFlow(2)` which applies `styleSteps[2]` - After that resolves, it waits 100ms and then calls `nestedFlow(3)` which resolves immediately (index >= styleSteps.length) Each `applyStyleStep` takes about 1000ms + 300ms = 1300ms to complete. 5. The final step applied is `styleSteps[2]`: ``` { '--bg-final': '#3498db', '--color-final': '#fff', '--font-size-final': '24px', '--transform-final': 'rotate(-1deg) scale(0.98)', '--text-shadow-final': '2px 2px 3px black', '--letter-spacing-final': '0.12em', '--line-height-final': '1.9', '--radius-final': '18px' } ``` 6. Now, the JS sets inline styles using `box.style.setProperty()`. These inline styles override the CSS rule's values. 7. The final values will be a combination of: - CSS rule values for properties NOT set by JS - JS inline style values for properties that ARE set by JS Let me check which properties are set by the JS in the final step (styleSteps[2]): - `--bg-final`: #3498db (JS) - `--color-final`: #fff (JS) - `--font-size-final`: 24px (JS) - `--transform-final`: rotate(-1deg) scale(0.98) (JS) - `--text-shadow-final`: 2px 2px 3px black (JS) - `--letter-spacing-final`: 0.12em (JS) - `--line-height-final`: 1.9 (JS) - `--radius-final`: 18px (JS) NOT set by the final JS step: - `--shadow-final`: stays from CSS rule = `0 0 20px #5e17eb` - `--border-color-final`: stays from CSS rule = `cyan` Wait, but the JS also sets properties in earlier steps. Let me reconsider... Actually, the JS applies each step sequentially, and later steps override earlier ones. The final state after all steps complete is determined by the last step (styleSteps[2]), plus any properties that were set in earlier steps but NOT overridden in later steps. So the final values are: - --bg-final: #3498db (from JS step 2) - --color-final: #fff (from JS step 2) - --font-size-final: 24px (from JS step 2) - --shadow-final: 0 0 8px #e67e22 (from JS step 1, not overridden in step 2) - --transform-final: rotate(-1deg) scale(0.98) (from JS step 2) - --text-shadow-final: 2px 2px 3px black (from JS step 2) - --letter-spacing-final: 0.12em (from JS step 2) - --line-height-final: 1.9 (from JS step 2) - --radius-final: 18px (from JS step 2) - --border-color-final: #d35400 (from JS step 1, not overridden in step 2) These are inline styles set via `setProperty`, so they override the CSS rule values.
